source.title: Python standard: move the base image to a pinned Python 3.15

labels.name: area/base

milestone.title: Trivy renewal 2026-11
milestone.description:
Renew or retire the Trivy exceptions in `.trivyignore.yaml` before they expire on 2026-12-01, after which Trivy stops honouring them and any finding still present blocks publishing, the weekly rebuild included. Also make the next lapse visible before it lands, and fix the image prose the tofu and node bumps left stale. Ships as: a node image rebuild for its corrected LABEL; the renewal itself changes no image.

**Build order:**
1. #484: re-scan against the current pins, remove exceptions that no longer match, and renew the rest at most 30 days out.
2. #427: warn before exceptions expire, and stop renewing them all to one date.
3. #329: check whether the tofu 1.13.2 bump already covered it; close it if so, otherwise add the missing 1.13.1 history line.
4. #477 + #459, one PR: the node image's Node 26 prose and LABEL, and the image comments that still mean the legacy template.

**Model per phase** (`models:` in .ai/project.yml):
- Plan: #427 needs your pick between its early-warning and stagger options (or both) before it is built; the rest needs no plan.
- Build: `sonnet` for all.
- Critic gate: `architect` + `security-critic` for `.trivyignore.yaml` and `.github/` changes (items 1 and 2); `architect` for the Dockerfile changes (items 3 and 4).
- Architect review: `opus`, fresh session.
- HITL: merges, and the #427 option pick.

source.body:
## Problem

The maintainer wants every Python project across glunk-works and 603-Identity on Python 3.15. This template defines the Python standard for consuming repos, so the move starts here.

Today the standard is Ubuntu's system Python:
- `images/base/Dockerfile`: "Ubuntu 26.04. Its system Python 3.14 is the Python standard for consuming repos. The major tracks GitHub's `ubuntu-latest` runner. Re-pin it deliberately, together with tests/smoke.sh's Python check."
- `tests/smoke.sh` checks `python3` is 3.14.
- `images/base/tools/pyproject.toml` declares `requires-python = ">=3.14"` for the tools every devcontainer carries.
- `docs/threat_model.md` lists uv-provisioned interpreters as a run-time download that is not part of the image and is never scanned.

Ubuntu 26.04 ships 3.14, and `ubuntu-latest` stays on 26.04, so 3.15 cannot come from the system package. Reaching 3.15 means the standard stops being "the runner's system Python".

## Proposed

A deliberate change of the standard, recorded as a decision in this repository:
- **Install a pinned 3.15 in the base image** as the default `python3` for consuming repos. The source (a uv-managed or python-build-standalone build) is pinned by version and sha256, the way `uv` itself is installed today. Ubuntu's system 3.14 stays only for apt's own tools.
- **Restate the rule.** The Dockerfile comment and the decision record name a pinned interpreter version instead of "tracks the runner's system Python". Consuming repos' CI uses `actions/setup-python` at the same version.
- **Same change, alongside it:** update `tests/smoke.sh`'s Python check to 3.15. Move `images/base/tools` (its `requires-python` and `uv.lock`) to 3.15, or say why it stays.
- **`docs/threat_model.md`:** say that the interpreter is now part of the image, so it is hashed at build and covered by the image scan, unlike a run-time uv download.
- Ships as a new image release. Consuming repos pick it up when they bump their template pin.

Design choices for the spec to settle: which build source to pin; how `python3` and `python` resolve when two interpreters are present; whether anything in the image relies on apt's Python being the default.

## Consuming repos to move after the release (checklist, tracked here)

Each moves in its own repository, with these changes:
- `.python-version`, `requires-python`, CI `python-version`, `FROM python:` lines and ruff `target-version` set to 3.15;
- its compiled dependencies confirmed to publish 3.15 wheels.

Where the timing lines up, each move is combined with that repo's template move. The order:
- [ ] glunk-works/scope-core first: the shared library. Decide whether its `requires-python` floor stays lower while CI tests 3.15.
- [ ] glunk-works/bounty-infra and glunk-works/loop-orchestrator together: their scope-core pins move as a pair. bounty-infra's runtime image and CI move ahead as a pilot in its own issue.
- [ ] glunk-works/resume-orchestrator
- [ ] glunk-works/bedrock-serverless-rag
- [ ] 603-Identity/checkov-ledger-action (check `checkov`'s 3.15 support first)
- [ ] the private 603-Identity repos, each checked for Python at its turn

## Out of scope

- Each consuming repo's own change, filed there.
- Node, Go or OpenTofu versions.

## Done when

- The base image's default `python3` is 3.15, pinned by version and hash, and the smoke check pins 3.15.
- The decision and threat model state the new standard.
- A release carries it.

spec-task: issue=556 base=main sha=ad63b2865a2ab7574c91876d95f8e9245e8c6fcb

Spec for #556: move the base image's default Python to a pinned 3.15. This comment is the whole spec: the builder never reads the issue body, so everything the build needs from it is restated below.
Critic gate: architect, security-critic, docs-consistency; 2 rounds; converged.

### Goal

Today the Python standard for consuming repos is Ubuntu 26.04's system Python 3.14, an apt package the weekly `apt-get upgrade` rebuild keeps patched. Ubuntu 26.04 and GitHub's `ubuntu-latest` stay on 3.14, so a 3.15 standard cannot come from apt. This task changes the standard deliberately: the base image installs a pinned CPython 3.15 build from astral-sh/python-build-standalone, verified by version and sha256 the way `uv` is installed today, and makes it the default `python3` (and `python`) for everything that resolves the name through `PATH`. Ubuntu's 3.14 stays at its apt path for apt's own tools and for the image's tools venv, which cannot move yet (see the Dockerfile bullet below for the reason). The rule is restated as a pinned interpreter version in the Dockerfile comment and in a new decision, DEVC-D11. The threat model records what this changes: the interpreter is now part of the image layer, fixed by its sha256 at build, instead of a run-time uv download, but it is also no longer refreshed by the weekly apt rebuild, and the image scan covers only the components Trivy actually identifies in it, which the build observes and records rather than assumes. Every derived image (`tofu`, `node`, `devapp`, `devapp-tofu`) inherits it from base.

### Files touched

- `images/base/Dockerfile`
  - Rewrite the comment that today reads "Ubuntu 26.04. Its system Python 3.14 is the Python standard for consuming repos. The major tracks GitHub's `ubuntu-latest` runner. Re-pin it deliberately, together with tests/smoke.sh's Python check." Keep the sentence that the Ubuntu major tracks the runner. Replace the Python sentence: the Python standard is now the pinned interpreter installed below (its version in the new ARG); Ubuntu's 3.14 stays only for apt's own tools and the tools venv; re-pin the interpreter deliberately, together with the smoke test's major.minor checks and DEVC-D11.
  - Leave the apt package list unchanged (`python3` and `python3-venv` stay).
  - Add a new block after the uv block and before the tools venv's `COPY`, with three new ARGs: `PYTHON_VERSION` **(new)**, `PYTHON_BUILD` **(new)** (the python-build-standalone release tag) and `PYTHON_SHA256` **(new)**. Use 3.15.2 from release 20261110, the newest 3.15 build when this spec was drafted, or a newer 3.15.x build if one exists when you build. The asset is the `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu-install_only_stripped.tar.gz` build of that version. Its sha256 is read from that release's own published `SHA256SUMS` asset (the same "sha256, two spaces, filename" format the other binaries' checksum files use), never computed from a first download. In the download URL, the `+` between version and build tag is written `%2B`.
  - The RUN downloads the tarball to a temp file, checks it with `sha256sum -c`, creates `/opt/devc` with `install -d -m 0755` (the block runs before the tools `COPY` that creates it today, and `tar -C` needs it to exist), extracts the tarball with `tar --no-same-owner` into `/opt/devc` (the archive's top directory is `python`, giving `/opt/devc/python`), and removes the tarball. `--no-same-owner` matters: without it, tar running as root keeps the archive's own uid, which could be 1000, the `app` user.
  - In the same RUN, delete pip from the extracted tree (the `pip` package and its dist-info under the interpreter's `site-packages`, and every `pip*` entry under its `bin`). Ubuntu's Python has no pip module today (the apt list installs no `python3-pip`), so this keeps today's surface: `python3 -m pip` fails as it does now. `python3 -m venv` still gives each venv its own pip from the stdlib's bundled `ensurepip` wheel.
  - In the same RUN, write a PEP 668 `EXTERNALLY-MANAGED` file into the interpreter's stdlib directory, as Ubuntu's own Python carries one, so installers that honour it (`uv pip install --system`, for one) refuse to write into the image's interpreter.
  - In the same RUN, create root-owned symlinks `/usr/local/bin/python3`, `/usr/local/bin/python3.15` and `/usr/local/bin/python` pointing at the new interpreter's `bin/python3.15`. `/usr/local/bin` precedes `/usr/bin` on `PATH`, so a bare `python3` or `python` (and an `env python3` shebang) resolves to 3.15, while apt's scripts keep their absolute `/usr/bin/python3` shebangs and stay on 3.14. Do not install any other entry point on `PATH`.
  - Update the uv block's comment, which today says uv provisions an older interpreter only for a repo whose `.python-version` asks for one and that the image carries no alternate interpreter. The new text: the image carries two interpreters (the pinned 3.15 and Ubuntu's 3.14); uv downloads one only when neither satisfies the request (another minor, or an exact patch other than the pinned one); and uv's default preference for interpreters it manages means one already installed in the home volume is used ahead of the image's.
  - The tools venv step (`uv sync --locked ... --python /usr/bin/python3`) keeps Ubuntu's interpreter. Add to its comment why: pre-commit depends on PyYAML, whose current release (6.0.3, the one `uv.lock` resolves) publishes no CPython 3.15 wheel, and the step refuses source builds (`--no-build`). The tools venv moves to 3.15 when the lock can resolve a 3.15 wheel for every package. A consequence worth one clause: pre-commit's own Python hooks default to the interpreter pre-commit runs on, so they run on 3.14 unless a repo sets `default_language_version`.
- `tests/smoke.sh`
  - Replace the `python3` 3.14 check with a hardcoded 3.15 major.minor check (the standard), plus an exact check of `python3`'s full version against a new `EXPECT_PYTHON` **(new)** environment variable.
  - Add checks that `command -v python3` is `/usr/local/bin/python3`; that `python`, `python3.15` and `python3` resolve to the same real interpreter path; that `/usr/bin/python3` is still 3.14 (the tools venv's interpreter); that no file under the new interpreter's directory is owned by anyone but root or is writable by group or others (symlinks excluded); that `python3 -c 'import pip'` fails; that the `EXTERNALLY-MANAGED` file exists in its stdlib directory; and that `UV_PYTHON_DOWNLOADS=never uv python find 3.15` succeeds and prints a path outside the app user's home directory.
  - Rewrite the header comment's "One is hardcoded below, by design: the system Python's major.minor" sentence. Two major.minor values are now hardcoded by design, and the header names both and why: 3.15, the Python standard for consuming repos; and 3.14, Ubuntu's apt Python, which the tools venv is built on. The 3.15 patch comes from the Dockerfile ARG like every other pin.
  - The existing `python3 -c` hashlib line that derives the betterleaks test token stays as is; it now runs on 3.15.
- `.github/scripts/build-and-test.sh`
  - Export `EXPECT_PYTHON` read with the existing `arg` helper from base's `PYTHON_VERSION`, add it to the loop that fails on an empty expected value, and pass it with `-e EXPECT_PYTHON` in the `smoke` function's `docker run`.
- `docs/roadmap.md`
  - Add DEVC-D11 after DEVC-D10, before the IAC-D citation table, with a status line, Context, Decision, Alternatives rejected, Consequences, and a "Why DEVC-D and not IAC-D" paragraph.
  - Decision, limited to what this repo's images ship and check: the base image's default `python3` and `python` are a pinned interpreter version (3.15) from python-build-standalone, pinned by version and sha256 from the release's own checksum file, with pip removed and a PEP 668 marker; Ubuntu's 3.14 stays for apt and the tools venv; the smoke test pins the major.minor; re-pin deliberately.
  - Alternatives rejected, each in one line: Ubuntu's apt Python (3.14 only on 26.04); `uv python install` at build time (its sha256 table lives inside the uv binary, so the interpreter pin would move with every uv bump instead of on its own line); building CPython from source in the image (build time and a compiler toolchain in the image); a run-time uv download (outside the image and its build-time hash).
  - Consequences: the default interpreter and the libraries built into it are refreshed by no weekly rebuild and bumped by no automation (`bump-binaries.sh` and Dependabot do not know it), so a security fix in CPython or its bundled libraries reaches the image only by a hand re-pin; the image scan covers only what the Trivy observation in Done when found; the tools venv stays on 3.14 until PyYAML ships a 3.15 wheel; a repo that already installed a 3.15 through uv keeps using that home-volume copy until it is uninstalled or the volume is wiped. Also, as a consumer obligation this entry cites but does not decide: consuming repos' CI is expected to use `actions/setup-python` at the same version, and that rule belongs in an IAC-D entry in infrastructure-core's log, pending, with each repo's move tracked on #556.
  - "Why DEVC-D and not IAC-D", following DEVC-D9's pattern: this entry records only what this repo publishes and checks; what consuming repos must do is cited, not decided, and is left to the pending IAC-D entry, as DEVC-D1 requires for a toolchain version other repos follow.
- `docs/threat_model.md`
  - Untrusted inputs table, "Release binaries" row: add the interpreter to the list, pinned by version and sha256 from python-build-standalone's own `SHA256SUMS`, and say it is re-pinned by hand only, since no automated bump knows it.
  - Rewrite the "uv-provisioned interpreters" row in both places it goes stale: its "Enters through" cell ("when a repo's `.python-version` asks for an older Python") and its last sentence ("Only a repo that cannot use the system 3.14 does this"). The new text: uv downloads an interpreter only when neither the image's pinned 3.15 nor Ubuntu's 3.14 satisfies the request (another minor, or an exact patch other than the pinned one); and an interpreter uv already installed in the home volume is preferred over the image's by uv, and its `python3.X` entry in `~/.local/bin` shadows the image's on `PATH`, until it is uninstalled or the volume is wiped.
  - Boundary 7 ("OS security fixes arrive on a schedule"): name the exception. The image's default `python3` is no longer an apt package, so the weekly rebuild does not refresh it.
  - Known gaps: add a bullet that the default interpreter and the libraries python-build-standalone links into it (OpenSSL among them) are frozen at the pin, refreshed by no rebuild and bumped by no automation, and say what the image scan covers in it, worded from the Trivy observation in Done when (if Trivy identifies no CPython component, say so plainly).
  - Known gaps, the bullet that lists what each ARG-pinned upstream publishes to check its checksum file: add python-build-standalone, stating only what its release page actually publishes for that (look at the release when you build; do not assume a signature or attestation exists). If it publishes nothing, amend the bullet's lead sentence ("Every ARG-pinned upstream publishes a way to check this") so it stays true, and keep python-build-standalone out of the closing sentence's 2026-10-02 confirmation, which predates the pin.
  - The smoke-test row of the controls table: replace "the system Python isn't the expected major.minor" with the new checks (the image's `python3` isn't the pinned version, the names don't resolve to it, or its files are writable by or owned by someone other than root).
- `README.md`
  - Image table, base row: "Python (system)" becomes "Python 3.15 (pinned)".
  - The sentence "Dependabot handles the base image digest, the GitHub Actions pins, and the Python tool lock": add one sentence after it saying that the Python interpreter's three ARGs in `images/base/Dockerfile` are moved by neither Dependabot nor `bump-binaries.sh`, so they are re-pinned by hand from the release's `SHA256SUMS`, together with the smoke test's major.minor check when the minor changes (DEVC-D11).

### Done when

- `bash .github/scripts/build-and-test.sh local` builds all five images, and every flavour's smoke run passes, including the new Python checks.
- In the built base image, `python3 --version` prints exactly the version in `PYTHON_VERSION` (3.15.x), `command -v python3` prints `/usr/local/bin/python3`, `python --version` matches it, `/usr/bin/python3 --version` still prints 3.14.x, and `python3 -m pip --version` fails.
- The interpreter's download is checked by `sha256sum -c` against `PYTHON_SHA256` in the Dockerfile, and that value equals the asset's line in the pinned release's `SHA256SUMS`.
- The build's Trivy image gate passes with no new entry in `.trivyignore.yaml`. If the gate flags something in the interpreter, stop and report it on the PR rather than adding an exception.
- The pinned Trivy image that `build-and-test.sh` uses, run with `image --list-all-pkgs --format json` against the locally built base image, has been read, and the PR description records which packages it lists under `/opt/devc/python` (or that it lists none). The threat-model and DEVC-D11 wording about scan coverage matches that record.
- hadolint, the Trivy misconfiguration scan, shellcheck and the gate tests in `.ai/project.yml`'s green gate all pass.
- `docs/roadmap.md` carries DEVC-D11; `docs/threat_model.md` and `README.md` say what is stated above; a search of `images/`, `tests/`, `README.md` and `docs/` (release notes excepted) finds no remaining claim that the system 3.14 is the Python standard.

### Tests

- New checks in `tests/smoke.sh`, listed under Files touched. They run against every flavour through `build-and-test.sh`'s `smoke` function.
- Existing suites that must still pass: the whole local green gate in `.ai/project.yml` (hadolint, Trivy config, shellcheck, devc-verify's `go test`, `tools/tests/run-gate-tests.sh`, zizmor, `build-and-test.sh local`, `tests/template-proof.sh`), and `tests/smoke-devapp.sh` for the two dev-App flavours.

### Out of scope

- Moving the tools venv (`images/base/tools/pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock`) to 3.15. Both stay unchanged; the reason goes in the Dockerfile comment and DEVC-D11.
- Teaching `bump-binaries.sh`, its workflow or Dependabot to bump the interpreter.
- Removing apt's `python3` or `python3-venv`, or changing uv's settings (`UV_PYTHON_DOWNLOADS`, python preference) in the image.
- Tagging the release, writing its notes under `docs/releases/`, and publishing the GitHub Release: a maintainer does these after merge, per README's "Cutting a release".
- Every consuming repo's own move (its `.python-version`, `requires-python`, CI `python-version`, `FROM python:` lines and ruff `target-version`), and this repo's own `.devcontainer/Dockerfile` image pin. #556 tracks that checklist.
- Any IAC-D entry in infrastructure-core's log, and `docs/adopting.md`.
- Node, Go or OpenTofu versions.

### Restated from the issue body

- The base image's default `python3` becomes a pinned 3.15, pinned by version and sha256 the way `uv` is installed; Ubuntu's 3.14 stays for apt's tools.
- The Dockerfile comment and a decision record state a pinned interpreter version instead of the runner's system Python. Choice: the issue also asks the decision to say consuming repos' CI uses `actions/setup-python` at the same version; because DEVC-D1 puts a rule other repos must follow in infrastructure-core's IAC-D log, DEVC-D11 cites that rule as a pending IAC-D obligation instead of deciding it, and the Dockerfile comment does not carry it.
- The smoke test's Python check moves to 3.15.
- The tools venv either moves to 3.15 or the change says why it stays. Choice: it stays on 3.14, because PyYAML 6.0.3 has no 3.15 wheel and the install refuses source builds. This also means Ubuntu's 3.14 serves the tools venv, not only apt's tools, which differs from the issue's wording.
- The threat model says the interpreter is now part of the image, hashed at build, unlike a run-time uv download. The issue also says it is covered by the image scan; this draft has the build observe what Trivy identifies in it and word the claim from that, and adds the loss of weekly apt patching, which the issue does not mention.
- Choice (the issue left it to the spec): the build source is python-build-standalone's `install_only_stripped` x86_64 build, with its sha256 taken from the release's `SHA256SUMS`, installed under `/opt/devc/python`.
- Choice (the issue left it to the spec): `python3`, `python3.15` and `python` resolve to the new interpreter through symlinks in `/usr/local/bin`; nothing else in the image relies on apt's Python being the default, because apt's tools use absolute `/usr/bin/python3` shebangs and the tools venv names `/usr/bin/python3` explicitly.
- Choice (not in the issue): pip is removed from the image's interpreter, matching today's pip-less Ubuntu Python, a PEP 668 marker is added, and `tar --no-same-owner` keeps the interpreter root-owned.
- The issue's "a release carries it" is split: this task lands the image change, and the tag and release notes follow after merge as a maintainer step.
- The consuming-repo checklist and each repo's own change stay out of scope; Node, Go and OpenTofu versions are out of scope.

### Not applied (tightenings)

Tightenings the critic gate did not apply. They are optional notes for the builder: following one is not a departure from this spec, and leaving one out is not a miss.

- Files touched, the Dockerfile's tools venv comment: its phrase about the tools landing on "the system interpreter" becomes ambiguous once the image has two system-wide interpreters; naming Ubuntu's 3.14 at its apt path would be clearer (docs-consistency).
- Files touched, the Dockerfile's new RUN: the smoke check that nothing under the interpreter is writable by group or others depends on the archive's own modes, because tar running as root keeps them; adding `--no-same-permissions` or a recursive `chmod go-w` on the interpreter directory would make the build enforce what the test asserts (architect, docs-consistency).
- Files touched, the Dockerfile's symlink bullet: the claim that a bare `python3` resolves to 3.15 holds only while nothing in `~/.local/bin`, which leads `PATH`, shadows it; the comment could say so (docs-consistency).
- Files touched, the threat model's uv-interpreters row: a `python3.X` entry in `~/.local/bin` comes only from an explicit `uv python install` (and bare `python3` and `python` only with its `--default` flag), not from a download `uv sync` or `uv run` makes on its own; the row could say that instead of implying every home-volume interpreter shadows the image's (architect).
- Files touched, the threat model's smoke-test row: the replacement text lists only the version, name and ownership checks; it could list every new Python check the smoke test adds (the pip refusal, the PEP 668 marker, Ubuntu's 3.14 at its apt path, and the uv lookup) so the controls table matches the test (architect, docs-consistency).
- Files touched, `tests/smoke.sh`: an offline check that the interpreter's TLS context loads CA certificates from the image's store would catch a bundled OpenSSL that cannot find it (architect).
- Files touched, `README.md`: the interpreter note could sit beside the bump section's statement of which tools `bump-binaries.yml` does not cover, and that section's "nothing else to edit there" could be qualified for the hardcoded Python minor; separately, the "Toolchain versions must match CI" section names only OpenTofu and Node and could gain one Python sentence pointing at DEVC-D11, or the spec's out-of-scope list could say why it stays as is (architect, docs-consistency).
